scope: analysis branch only; main GEB unchanged
prior_research: Floristic homogenization among geographically distant, climatically similar regions is already known (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-27603-y); direct repetition is not novel.
question: Does the geographic identity of added potential larval resources preferentially connect distant, latitudinally analogous butterfly resource assemblages beyond fixed addition margins?
primary: (mean contemporary-minus-native regional butterfly-resource Jaccard for far cross-Level1 lat-analog pairs) minus same gain for far cross-Level1 lat-discordant pairs

null.method: butterfly×WGSRPD3 introduced addition edge swaps only within WGSRPD Level1; native incidences forbidden
preserves: added regions per butterfly per Level1

pass: Observed primary > null median and one-sided Monte Carlo p<=0.05
fail: Do not promote homogenization as selective if gate fails; no retuning bin boundaries after inspection.
boundaries: Latitude and WGSRPD Level1 are crude proxies, not measured climate and formal biogeographic realms.
Region pairs are dependent; inference from incidence randomization, not number of pairs.
Even a positive result is potential resource geography, not butterfly colonization, use, abundance, competition or fitness.
Require independent climate and plant-flora benchmark before any stand-alone ecological interpretation.
